title: The Geometry of Lee-Yang Tensors
abstract: We provide a geometric description of Lee-Yang tensors, building upon several recent results of Bravyi, Gosset, Liu, and Wong. By applying tools from complex Perron-Frobenius theory, we generalize one of their key lemmas to bound the spectral ratio of non-normal operators with Lee-Yang radius greater than one. As a direct consequence, we provide a local-to-global principle for bounding spectral gaps of Suzuki-Fisher Hamiltonians, a family of $2$-local Hamiltonians, using only the Lee-Yang radius of each local operator to bound the gap from below. On the other hand, we develop a simple perturbative technique to show that the Gibbs states of $k$-local Hamiltonians, $k \geq 3$, cannot have Lee-Yang radius at least one for all inverse temperatures $β\geq 0$. We apply this same method to conclude that Suzuki-Fisher Hamiltonians are precisely those Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states are Lee-Yang at all inverse temperatures $β\geq 0$.
summary: This work develops a geometric understanding of Lee-Yang tensors to analyze the spectral properties of quantum Hamiltonians. It establishes a local-to-global principle for bounding spectral gaps in specific Hamiltonians, most notably the Suzuki-Fisher class. The research provides a rigorous characterization of these Hamiltonians based on the persistence of their Lee-Yang radius across all inverse temperatures.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a geometric description of Lee-Yang tensors and use this framework to establish powerful local-to-global principles for bounding spectral gaps in quantum many-body systems.
main_result: It proves a local-to-global principle for bounding spectral gaps of Suzuki-Fisher Hamiltonians using only the Lee-Yang radius of local operators, and characterizes these Hamiltonians based on their Gibbs state properties.
method: The methodology combines complex Perron-Frobenius theory with the analysis of generating polynomials associated with the Lee-Yang radius, leading to asymptotic and perturbative constraints on the Hamiltonian structure.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum many-body systems described by $k$-local Hamiltonians, particularly the Suzuki-Fisher family of 2-local Hamiltonians, and their associated Gibbs states $\exp(- eta H)$.
key_observables: Lee-Yang radius ($r$), Spectral Gap, Spectral Ratio, and the generating polynomial $F_H(z, w)$.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), the locality $k$ of the Hamiltonian, and the radius $r$ of the Lee-Yang tensor.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on generalizing results from complex Perron-Frobenius theory and assumes the applicability of the local-to-global principle derived from the Lee-Yang radius.
paper_structure: The paper builds by generalizing spectral ratio bounds using complex Perron-Frobenius theory, deriving a local-to-global principle for spectral gaps, and then using perturbative techniques to characterize the class of Hamiltonians (Suzuki-Fisher) whose Gibbs states maintain a large Lee-Yang radius for all $ eta \ge 0$.
why_interesting: The connection between spectral properties (gaps) and analytic properties (Lee-Yang radius) provides a powerful, non-standard diagnostic tool for understanding quantum phase transitions and the stability of ground states in interacting quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The roots of the univariate polynomial Fexp(−βH)(s, . . . , s) for a k-local Hamiltonian of the form H = I −|ψ⟩⟨ψ|, where |ψ⟩= |0⟩⊗k. For k = 2, the resulting Hamiltonian is Suzuki-Fisher and hence its roots avoid the interior of the unit disk, but for all k ≥3, roots shatter symmetrically from s = i for sufficiently small β > 0, ensuring that at least one enters the interior of the disk.
